text:
Julia: quick sync — ran long-context kv-cache soak and saw steady memory growth + lots of tiny free holes. attaching notes below.
Sahil: hmm, growth as in RSS increasing over time?
Julia: yes, ~120MB -> 420MB over 2h on a 16k sequence workload, while token throughput stable.
Marc: can you paste the small profiler dump?
Julia: pasted sample from `kvprof` run:
```
free-buckets: 8123
alloc-buckets: 1967
avg-block-size: 8192
block-count: 12000
largest-free-run: 5 blocks
compaction-invocations: 2
```
Anya: avg-block-size 8k stands out. Are we splitting big slab allocations into small units?
Julia: yes — stride allocator currently shards 64k pages into 8k blocks for LRU reuse. This increases fragmentation on mixed-length KV entries (some are 2k, some 40k).
Kevin: that aligns with the 'scatter' pattern I saw in the binary heap traces — many small holes between used blocks.
Sahil: does compaction run on allocation path or background?
Julia: background thread every 30s but it only compacts runs >= 16 contiguous free blocks. with 8k block size, most holes are 1-3 blocks so never compacted.
Marc: possible quick fixes: bump block unit to 16k/32k, decrease compaction threshold to 3 blocks, or implement hole coalescing on free. each has tradeoffs.
Anya: can we synthesize tradeoffs experimentally? small block size helps reuse of small entries and reduces internal waste; big blocks reduce fragmentation but cause internal slack for small entries.
Julia: ran two microbench variants: `block=8k,compaction>=16` vs `block=32k,compaction>=4`. results over 1h soak on 4 workers:
```
8k/16: rss_end=420MB, avg-alloc-lat=0.82ms, cache-hit=96.4%
32k/4: rss_end=210MB, avg-alloc-lat=1.1ms, cache-hit=96.0%
```
Sahil: interesting — 32k cut memory growth ~2x but allocation latency +30%.
Kevin: 1.1ms is still acceptable for our 50ms tail SLOs, especially if it keeps instance counts lower.
Marc: what's CPU overhead for compaction more frequent?
Julia: `compaction>=4` increased compaction CPU by ~12% in profiling (mostly memcpy/scan). but net CPU per token decreased because fewer page faults and less GC churn.
Anya: any regressions in p99 latency?
Julia: p99 stable within noise for attach workload, but we need to check bursty patterns.
Sahil: can we try hybrid: keep 8k base for small live allocations but maintain a quick coalesce path that merges adjacent free blocks even if <4, triggered opportunistically by background idle windows?
Marc: aka opportunistic coalescing — low-latency path that only touches header bitmasks and merges without shifting data. then trigger full compaction only when contiguous run length above threshold.
Julia: prototype implemented: `coalesce-on-free` + `compaction-threshold=8`. test results (1h):
```
8k/coalesce: rss_end=250MB, avg-alloc-lat=0.9ms, compaction-cpu+6%/overall cpu -3%
```
Kevin: that looks promising — good middle ground.
Anya: are there edge-cases where coalescing might introduce fragmentation metadata blowup? e.g., lots of tiny allocations freed rapidly?
Julia: coalesce only updates bitmap and doubly-linked freelist; worst-case path is O(1) per free. we validated in synthetic churn test (10k alloc/frees/s) and saw stable metadata size.
Sahil: deployment plan? A/B on canary pool with 2k sequence jobs and 64k sequence jobs. watch RSS slope, p50/p95/p99, and CPU compaction counters.
Marc: add a metric for "free-run-distribution" buckets (1,2,3-7,8-15,16+) so we can validate shift after changes.
Julia: already added. pushing patch to `kv/allocator/coalesce` branch. PR incoming.
ops-bot: deploy request queued — canary group: runtime-canary-3. Please confirm when ready.
Sahil: I can run canary tomorrow morning. will schedule 6am PT and watch 4h soak.
Julia: thanks — PR link in thread when opened. tagging @Marc @Anya for review. :thumbsup:
Kevin: small note: update docs on expected block-size knobs in runtime config and default compaction values.
Julia: will include.
Sahil: great work team, this feels like a low-risk perf win with measurable memory savings.
